procedure.description: infliximab injection, 10 mg units, induction for moderate to severe Crohn disease

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for HCPCS J1745 (infliximab injection, 10 mg units, induction for moderate to severe Crohn disease) with date of service 2026-04-05. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish failure of conventional therapy as required by the step therapy policy.

criteria.text: Moderately to severely active Crohn disease documented by a Harvey-Bradshaw Index of 8 or more (or Crohn Disease Activity Index of 220 or more), or endoscopic evidence of active disease.

Inadequate response, intolerance, or contraindication to conventional therapy with a corticosteroid course and an immunomodulator (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, or methotrexate), unless the disease is fistulizing.
Negative tuberculosis and hepatitis B screening before the first dose.
Prescribed by or in consultation with a gastroenterologist, at weight-based dosing of 5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6 for induction.

chart.text: Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 228, LDL 114, HDL 52, triglycerides 125. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
Blood pressure check. 118 over 84 today, 136 over 79 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.

Colonoscopy with ileal intubation. Deep serpiginous ulcers with cobblestoning in the terminal ileum and ascending colon, normal rectum and left colon. Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn Disease 14. Biopsies taken.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Terminal ileum and ascending colon biopsies: chronic active ileocolitis with crypt distortion and a non-necrotizing granuloma. Consistent with Crohn disease.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Vitamin D came back 17. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 4 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

40 year old woman in gastroenterology follow-up for ileocolonic Crohn disease diagnosed 1 years ago. Missing work, up at night. Discussed moving to an anti-TNF agent, the infusion schedule, infection risk, and screening before the first dose. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives with her spouse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Harvey-Bradshaw Index 13 today: 5 liquid stools a day, abdominal pain most days, feels generally unwell, down 14 pounds in 3 months.

Prednisone 40 daily with a taper starting 7 months ago, flared at 10 milligrams; second taper 5 months ago, flared again at 15. Azathioprine 150 daily (2.5 per kilo) for 5 months with therapeutic metabolite levels and no improvement in the Harvey-Bradshaw Index. Mesalamine stopped as ineffective.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.6, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Interferon-gamma release assay negative. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative, core antibody negative, surface antibody positive from vaccination. Chest X-ray clear. Hepatitis C antibody negative.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Screening labs reviewed and negative. Consent for infliximab signed. First infusion scheduled next week; the prior authorization request went in today. Vitals today 134 over 80, pulse 74.
Infliximab induction dose 1, 300 milligrams (5 per kilo at 67 kilograms) intravenous over 2 hours per gastroenterology, premedicated, tolerated without reaction. Week 2 and week 6 doses scheduled.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
